source_snapshot.test_name: Test connections between BMC, HMC EROT, HMC I2C-1, FPGA 2 EROT and FPGA 2
source_snapshot.purpose_facts: From the BMC, address device 0x11 on Linux I2C adapter 1 with a two-byte write followed by a three-byte read and confirm that a reply is returned; PID 1114953 is referenced for other devices expected on the bus.
procedure_facts: Confirm the SUT configuration and clear relevant logs.
Run `i2ctransfer -y 1 w2@0x11 0x04 0x00 r3` and ensure a reply is returned.
criteria_facts: Collect results and photos in the designated location.
Check dmesg, syslog, SEL and other relevant logs for unexpected entries.
source_conflicts: The title names a multi-component BMC-to-HMC-to-FPGA-2 path, but the procedure observes only one address, 0x11; no source text establishes which component owns that address or whether its reply exercises every named hop.
The criterion requires only an unspecified reply and supplies neither the expected three bytes nor a mask/semantic rule, so ACK or arbitrary data cannot prove the stated path.
The broad `i2cdetect -q` scan can issue SMBus quick-write probes, while the source supplies no approved address matrix or device safety policy.
missing_source_information: PID 1114953 mapping of Linux adapter 1, address 0x11 and every named HMC/EROT/FPGA-2 hop.
Protocol meaning and state effect of bytes 0x04 0x00, expected three-byte response, masks and allowed variants.
Evidence showing whether the 0x11 response attests the complete chain or only a single endpoint.
Safe addresses/probe methods for bus 1, driver ownership, timeout, retry, recovery and photo type.

original_test_intent.statement: Functionally exercise the specified BMC-side I2C transaction toward address 0x11 and use the approved response plus PID 1114953 bus/path mapping to verify the intended connection path among the BMC, HMC EROT/HMC I2C-1 and FPGA 2 EROT/FPGA 2.
must_preserve: Linux I2C adapter 1 and target address 0x11, subject to signed platform mapping.
The exact two-byte write followed by three-byte read transaction after protocol approval.
The named BMC/HMC/EROT/FPGA-2 scope rather than an unrelated I2C endpoint.
PID 1114953 comparison, reply capture and unexpected-log review.
must_not_infer: That an ACK alone proves every named component or physical trace.
That 0x11 is an HMC EROT, FPGA EROT or other endpoint without PID mapping.
That 0x04 0x00 is a harmless register pointer or read selector rather than a state-changing command.
That physical probing, soldering or continuity inspection is required by the source.
That any three returned bytes constitute PASS without expected response semantics.

v2_review_conclusion.summary: V2 correctly warns that I2C visibility cannot by itself prove the complete named chain and that the write phase needs protocol approval.
v2_review_conclusion.specific_gap: V2 invents physical inspection, continuity/logic probing, probe equipment and board photos as the core test although the source specifies a BMC command/reply workflow. It therefore assigns MANUAL ONLY instead of separating resolvable platform/protocol inputs from automatable evidence collection.

related_records: Reliability row 127 uses a different bus, MUX and endpoint set; its command and mapping cannot be reused for this HMC/FPGA-2 path.
applicable_history.precedence_application: The exact source procedure controls the execution method, while the title controls the claimed scope. Their mismatch must remain SOURCE_CONFLICT until PID 1114953 proves what the single 0x11 response represents; older DeepSeek/V2 physical-probing assumptions are not source facts.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Reclassify the command-driven case from MANUAL ONLY to gated hybrid automation, but do not claim that one 0x11 reply validates the complete named chain. Execution requires PID path attribution, exact protocol/expected-response semantics and an approved safe access method; no physical probing is introduced.

conditions_present: BMC execution context, candidate adapter/address, exact transaction shape, PID reference, reply requirement and log/evidence collection are present.
missing: Adapter/address/path attribution, 0x04/0x00 command semantics and state effect, expected three-byte response, safe scan scope, driver ownership, timeout/retry, recovery and evidence-photo definition.
provider: Board/BMC/HMC/FPGA owner supplies PID 1114953, the signed bus/path/address map and protocol definition.
Test owner defines the expected response/mask and whether it attests each named hop.
Lab owner approves the maintenance window, direct userspace access and recovery.
safe_read_only_work: Record BMC, board, HMC, FPGA and firmware identities and collect existing SEL/system-log baselines without clearing them.
Use `i2cdetect -l`, sysfs I2C topology and driver bindings to map adapter 1 without probing devices.
Review PID 1114953 offline and capture existing kernel-enumerated clients at 0x11 without forcing access.
prohibited_until_resolved: `i2cdetect -q` or other broad scans, the 0x11 combined transaction, forced access, driver unbind, log clear, bus reset, physical probing, automatic retries or a PASS claim.
closure_evidence: Signed PID/topology evidence maps adapter 1 and 0x11 to the named path and states exactly which hops the reply validates.
Protocol documentation identifies the two written bytes, expected three returned bytes/mask, state effect and restoration if needed.
Owner-approved targeted access, timeout, retry prohibition, stop/recovery and acceptance rules are recorded.

revision_candidate.test_name: Verify BMC-to-HMC/FPGA-2 I2C Path Using the PID-Defined 0x11 Transaction
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify the PID-defined functional I2C path from the BMC toward the named HMC EROT/HMC I2C-1 and FPGA 2 EROT/FPGA 2 scope by executing the approved address-0x11 write-then-read request and comparing the three-byte response with its protocol-defined value. Claim only the hops that PID 1114953 states this response attests.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Only the board revision, BMC firmware, HMC/EROT/FPGA firmware and Linux I2C topology covered by PID 1114953. Execute from the BMC on the signed mapping of logical HMC I2C-1 to Linux adapter 1; do not reuse this address or response on another platform.
revision_candidate.target_scope: One mapped BMC adapter-1 path and the single PID-defined 7-bit endpoint at 0x11. The claimed chain is limited to components explicitly attested by that endpoint/protocol. Physical continuity, signal integrity, solder inspection, other adapters/addresses and unrelated HMC/FPGA functions are out of scope. Treat 15/5 minutes as estimates.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Board/BMC/HMC/FPGA revisions; PID 1114953; signed adapter-1 and 0x11 ownership/path map; 0x04 0x00 request definition; expected three-byte reply/mask and hop-attestation rule; state-change/restoration semantics; driver ownership; approved i2c-tools build; targeted-access policy; timeout and retry rule; evidence-photo definition; BMC access; maintenance authorization; bus/BMC recovery.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: From the BMC, preserve identities and pre-test logs, then record `i2cdetect -l`, sysfs topology, adapter functionality and the 0x11 binding without device probes. Do not run the source's broad `i2cdetect -y -q 1` unless PID explicitly authorizes every probe. After approval, execute exactly one `i2ctransfer -y 1 w2@0x11 0x04 0x00 r3` (or the owner-approved equivalent with identical combined-message semantics), capture the three bytes, exit status and timestamps, and compare them with the signed response rule. Verify any required state restoration and collect post-test bus/BMC/HMC/FPGA health and logs.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Exact platform identity matches PID; adapter 1 and 0x11 are mapped to the intended path; adapter supports the required combined transfer; no incompatible kernel driver or competing service owns the endpoint; command semantics, expected response, state effect, stop/recovery and evidence destination are approved; maintenance access and baseline health are confirmed.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Platform and firmware identities; PID revision; adapter/sysfs topology and binding evidence; 0x11 endpoint/path attribution; i2c-tools version and adapter functionality; pre-test health/log baseline; approval record; exact command, stdout/stderr, exit status and timestamps; all three reply bytes with mask/semantic comparison; documented hop coverage; state/restoration proof if applicable; post-test BMC/HMC/EROT/FPGA health and relevant SEL/system logs; engineer disposition.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: PID 1114953 plus the signed 0x11 endpoint protocol and expected-response definition for the exact platform revisions. Pass requires the approved three-byte response, no disallowed I2C/log/health effect and required restoration; it validates only the explicitly attributed functional path and does not prove physical continuity.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Do not infer endpoint identity from address alone, use a broad quick-write scan without an approved safe-address matrix, force access to a driver-owned endpoint, alter the request bytes, repeat automatically, clear evidence logs before preservation, probe/solder hardware or claim all named hops from ACK alone. Stop on mapping/protocol mismatch, NACK, timeout, bus busy/lock, unexpected bytes, device reset/state change, new relevant error, management impact or failed restoration.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Board/protocol owner approves PID mapping, command semantics, expected bytes and claimed hop coverage; lab owner approves direct BMC I2C access and recovery; test owner judges PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED and any deviation or rerun.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: No physical manipulation is required by the source. Humans provide protected artifacts, access and approvals and perform exceptional recovery. Once handed off, an Agent may collect topology, execute one approved targeted transaction, compare exact evidence and report without widening the claim.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: If the command changes endpoint state, perform only the signed restore operation and verify the original state. On bus lock, endpoint loss or management impact, stop transactions, preserve evidence and invoke the board owner's bus/BMC/HMC recovery; prove all affected components healthy before considering a rerun.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: PID, adapter/address/path map, protocol semantics, expected bytes/mask, state/restoration, ownership, approval, timeout or recovery is missing; platform identity differs; adapter lacks the required transfer capability; endpoint is incompatibly driver-owned; pre-health fails; command returns NACK/timeout/unexpected data; a bus/log/health anomaly appears; or restoration/final health cannot be proved.

identified_defects: V2 fabricates physical probing and continuity evidence not present in the source.
The single 0x11 reply is not mapped to the complete multi-hop scope named in the title.
The expected three-byte reply and comparison semantics are missing.
The write bytes may select a register or may change state; the source does not say which.
The unbounded `i2cdetect -q` step lacks device-specific scan safety.
Generic result photos do not establish a physical-inspection requirement.
reason_for_change: Remove the unsupported manual electrical-inspection test, preserve the actual BMC combined transaction, and expose the unresolved title-to-observation gap so the Agent cannot turn an arbitrary ACK or three bytes into proof of the full HMC/EROT/FPGA-2 chain.

new_technical_evidence.title: Implementing I2C Device Drivers in Userspace
new_technical_evidence.supports: Adapter numbers must be resolved through sysfs or `i2cdetect -l`, and combined write/read userspace transactions use I2C_RDWR semantics and require adapter capability.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The platform mapping and endpoint protocol remain private PID inputs.

new_technical_evidence.title: The I2C Protocol
new_technical_evidence.supports: A combined transaction consists of explicit write/read messages and repeated-start behavior; protocol meaning comes from the addressed device, not from the generic I2C transaction shape.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Whether 0x04 0x00 is a selector or mutation and what the three bytes mean are not public in this record.

new_technical_evidence.title: i2cdetect(8)
new_technical_evidence.supports: Bus probing can confuse devices and `-q` uses SMBus quick-write probes that are explicitly not recommended, so the broad scan needs a device-specific safe-address policy.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The BMC's installed i2c-tools version and safe bus-1 address matrix are unknown.

new_technical_evidence.title: Source testcase Wistron-HW Robust-00010-V002
new_technical_evidence.supports: The BMC execution point, adapter/address, exact request shape, PID reference, reply requirement and generic evidence steps.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Endpoint identity, complete path coverage, expected response and state effect are absent.

removed_ambiguities: Separates functional I2C response testing from unrequested physical continuity inspection.
Defines the command as one combined write-then-read transaction rather than a generic read.
Limits the connectivity claim to PID-attributed hops instead of assuming the title is fully observed.
Requires exact reply semantics and safe targeted access before execution.
resolved_blockers: Physical probing, soldering and continuity photography are removed as fabricated manual prerequisites; the defined command/evidence workflow becomes automatable after handoff.
remaining_blockers: The title/procedure scope conflict, address/path attribution, request/reply semantics, safe access method, ownership, approval and recovery must be resolved before the transaction or PASS judgment.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 converts an invented physical test into the source-defined BMC transaction while adding the missing proof boundary: one 0x11 response validates only PID-attributed hops and only when its exact three-byte meaning is known.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The contract-only validator preserved the single BMC-side combined transaction, exact mapped 0x11 scope and one-transaction limit; it rejected ACK/exit-status-only completion, broad scanning, physical-continuity claims and attribution to unsigned hops. It classified unresolved PID, mapping, reply semantics, ownership and recovery as platform handoff inputs rather than an irreducible document blocker.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: Reliability row 132 runs a two-byte write/three-byte read to 0x11 from BMC adapter 1 and asks only that a reply be returned, despite naming five path elements.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 notices that bus visibility cannot prove the chain but then replaces the command-defined test with manual probing and photos, causing MANUAL ONLY overclassification.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Permit topology and artifact reconciliation now; permit exactly one targeted combined transaction only after address/path attribution, protocol/expected bytes, ownership, approval and recovery are signed.
